how_it_works: A single fixed-width vertical rail runs down the left (or center on desktop) of the Experience section — a 1px maroon (#8B2E2A) hairline drawn as an SVG <line>/<path> with fill:none. Each career beat is a row anchored to the spine by a small date node (dot or ring) sitting on the line; the role/org content sits to the right of the rail (or alternates left/right on wide screens). The whole section is NOT pinned — it scrolls naturally with the page (page height = sum of beat heights), which avoids scroll-jacking and keeps recruiter skimming fast. Two motion layers ride the scroll: (1) the spine itself draws top-to-bottom via stroke-dashoffset (set strokeDasharray = strokeDashoffset = path.getTotalLength(), tween to 0) bound with ScrollTrigger scrub:1 from 'top 80%' to 'bottom 40%', so the hairline 'grows' as you read and acts as a reading-progress indicator; (2) each node + its content reveals ONCE on entry (opacity 0->1, y 24px->0, node scale 0.6->1) triggered per-row at 'top 75%' with toggleActions 'play none none none' — use ScrollTrigger.batch or a forEach over rows with stagger 0.08–0.12. Clinical beats (Andhra Medical College, and optionally the nference clinical-note extraction beat) get an extra ECG/weave accent: a small inline SVG heartbeat path next to the node that draws in once via stroke-dashoffset when that node enters. Scroll distance is content-driven (no forced +=3000 pin); the only scrub is the low-cost spine draw. Reverse-chronological order, current role first. On mobile the rail pins to the far left with a single content column; the alternating layout collapses to one side.
visual_structure: A single beat = [node on spine] + [content block]. Node: 8–10px maroon ring/dot centered on the 1px rail; the current/lead beat can use a slightly larger filled node to signal 'present'. Content block, top to bottom: date range in JetBrains Mono meta (e.g. 'Apr 2026 — Present', muted #5A5A5A), role title in Fraunces (serif, the visual anchor of the beat), org name in Inter (with continuity note for nference 'promoted from intern' handled as a sub-line under the same beat rather than a second full node), 2–3 tight Inter bullets or one proof line, and an optional mono proof chip (e.g. '~90% test acc' for DEXTER CXR). The maroon spine visually threads all beats into one continuous career path. Clinical beats (AMC bedside reality; optionally nference oncology clinical-note work) carry a subtle ECG hairline motif adjacent to the node — used sparingly (one or two beats, per Brand_Kit 'signature, not spam'). Beats stack vertically and do NOT morph into each other; they simply reveal in sequence as the spine draws past them. Optional alternating left/right placement on md+ for editorial rhythm, collapsing to a single right-of-rail column on mobile. Whitespace between beats is generous (editorial-minimal), letting the hairline breathe.
motion_recipe: GSAP + ScrollTrigger only (no framer-motion), matching existing primitives in src/components/text and src/components/work. Spine draw: gsap.set(spinePath,{strokeDasharray:L,strokeDashoffset:L}); gsap.to(spinePath,{strokeDashoffset:0,ease:'none',scrollTrigger:{trigger:'.timeline',start:'top 80%',end:'bottom 40%',scrub:1,invalidateOnRefresh:true}}). Node/content reveal: per-row ONCE, gsap.from(row,{opacity:0,y:24,duration:0.6,ease:'power2.out',scrollTrigger:{trigger:row,start:'top 75%',toggleActions:'play none none none'}}); prefer ScrollTrigger.batch for stagger:0.1 across visible rows. Node pop: scale 0.6->1 with slight overshoot (ease:'back.out(1.5)') on the same trigger. ECG accent on clinical beats: stroke-dashoffset draw-in once (~0.9s, ease:'power1.inOut') on node enter — no infinite loop/pulse (that reads gimmicky and burns battery). Section titles use existing BlurText entrance. DO NOT: pin/scrub the whole section (scroll-jack), animate width/height/layout (use transform+opacity for 60fps), infinitely loop the ECG, parallax the rail, or scrub the per-beat text reveals (reveals fire once, only the spine is scrubbed). Optional Lenis smooth-scroll synced via gsap.ticker.add(t=>lenis.raf(t*1000)) and lenis.on('scroll',ScrollTrigger.update) — gate behind the reduced-motion check.
reduced_motion: Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, render the fully-drawn state as a static resting layout — spine fully painted (strokeDashoffset:0, no draw tween), all nodes and content at opacity:1/y:0, ECG accents shown as a static drawn glyph (or omitted). Skip Lenis entirely and let native scroll handle it. The reverse-chronological rail with date nodes, roles, orgs and proof chips still communicates the whole career path with zero motion — nothing is hidden behind an animation, so the section is fully legible and the reading-progress affordance simply becomes a normal static timeline. Guard by wrapping all gsap/ScrollTrigger setup in a matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference)') branch (gsap.matchMedia()).
brand_fit: HIGH. This is arguably the most on-brand Experience pattern for the clinical-AI portfolio. Reasons: (1) The maroon #8B2E2A hairline spine is a literal expression of the Brand_Kit accent-as-seasoning rule and the dual-type system (Fraunces role + Inter body + JetBrains Mono dates). (2) The optional ECG accent on the AMC/clinical beat is exactly the 'quiet ECG hairline motif, one use not spam' signature already called out in the experience-work-landing spec. (3) It is editorial-minimal and reduced-motion-safe by construction — the once-reveals + single scrubbed spine avoid scroll-jack abuse and the 'every ReactBits effect at once' trap. (4) It delivers Karpathy-style institution credibility: named orgs (nference, Andhra Medical College, DEXTER) and multi-AMC cohorts read as a serious research/clinical trajectory threaded on one line, WITHOUT LinkedIn card chrome, logos, connection counts, or SaaS purple glow. Minor risk: a bare vertical timeline can read generic if the spine/nodes are default-styled — the maroon hairline, Fraunces roles, mono dates and the AMC ECG beat are what lift it out of template territory.
steal: Steal the maroon 1px spine that draws top-to-bottom on scroll AND doubles as a reading-progress indicator — bind it to ScrollTrigger scrub while every beat's text reveals only ONCE. This one detail (a scrubbed hairline over once-revealed content) gives the section motion and a sense of 'career path being traced' without any pin or scroll-jack, and it's the natural home for the signature ECG accent on the Andhra Medical College bedside beat.
avoid: Avoid pinning the section and scrubbing the beat content to the scroll position — turning a legible reverse-chron timeline into a slow scroll-jacked scrubber is recruiter-hostile (they can't skim, back-scroll re-triggers, and momentum feels broken). Also avoid an infinitely looping/pulsing ECG line: a perpetual heartbeat animation reads as a gimmick, competes with the text for attention, drains battery, and violates the 'signature not spam' rule — draw the ECG once on entry and let it rest.
live_examples: anurag-rai/portfolio-website (github.com/anurag-rai/portfolio-website) — Astro + GSAP developer portfolio with an Experience.astro 'vertical timeline powered by experience.ts, rendering a TimelineNode per entry with a scroll-synced progress line that tracks reading position' (closest direct match to the scrubbed-spine + per-node reveal model). [uncertain] For the 'institution credibility without LinkedIn' tone, karpathy.ai is the reference feel (prestigious orgs/advisors woven into flowing narrative text, no card chrome) though it is prose, not a literal vertical spine timeline. [uncertain] Codrops' Joffrey Spitzer portfolio (tympanus.net/codrops/2026/02/18/) demonstrates the minimalist Astro+GSAP reveal/scrub discipline this pattern relies on, but its showcase is a scaling vertical slider rather than a date-node career timeline.
